# Appendix D. `/proc/ish` reference

AOK's own addition to procfs — the guest asking about the app it is running
inside. Nothing on real Linux has it. Chapter 18 covers the design; this is the
inventory, generated from `fs/proc/ish.c`.

## Nodes

- `/proc/ish/amd64_jit` (file)
- `/proc/ish/amd64_jit_fuse` (file)
- `/proc/ish/amd_jit` (file)
- `/proc/ish/arm64_jit_fuse` (file)
- `/proc/ish/colors` (file)
- `/proc/ish/defaults` (directory)
- `/proc/ish/documents` (file)
- `/proc/ish/host_info` (file)
- `/proc/ish/i386_jit_fuse` (file)
- `/proc/ish/i386_no_cache_comm` (file)
- `/proc/ish/i386_single_step_comm` (file)
- `/proc/ish/ips` (file)
- `/proc/ish/riscv64_jit_fuse` (file)
- `/proc/ish/roots` (file)
- `/proc/ish/version` (file)
- `/proc/ish/workspace` (file)

## The ones that do more than report

- **`defaults/`** — one file per app preference, values as JSON. `0444`,
  root-writable; a write goes through the same validation the Settings
  screen uses, and removing an entry resets that preference (Chapter 18).
- **`<arch>_jit_fuse`** — the instruction-fusion mask, readable and writable
  at run time, consumed at translation time. The measurement surface behind
  Chapters 6 and 38.
- **`roots`** — the root manager. Reading lists roots, the catalogue and the
  current job; writing accumulates `key=value` lines until `run` (Chapter 30).
